newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FIORI ENDS DROUGHT AS TIGER FADES AT QUAD CITY CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FIORI ENDS DROUGHT AS TIGER FADES AT QUAD CITY CLASSIC.

text.p: Ed Fiori ended a 14-year victory drought on Sunday when he passed a faltering Tiger Woods and posted a two-stroke triumph at the $1.2 million Quad City Classic at the Oakwood Country Club.
The 43-year-old Fiori had not won since the 1982 Bob Hope Desert Classic but got back on top again with a three-under 67 that gave him a 72-hole total of 268, two shots better than Andrew Magee.

"My mind is numb," Fiori, 43, said. "I'm tired, exhausted. It hasn't really sunk in. I never thought I would be in this position again after 14 years. I actually sent my qualifying school application in and my wife and I discussed retirement."
Fiori earned $216,000 for his unlikely victory.

Fiori began the day one stroke behind Tiger Woods, contending for his first title in just his third tournament as a professional. But Woods fouled up with a quadruple bogey at the fourth hole on his way to a 72 and a tie for fifth.

"I let it slip away in a heartbeat," said Woods, who twice found water at the par-4 fourth. "I had a shot, I just didn't execute it. I felt like I had an opportunity. Mentally, I did a good job. Physically, I made mistakes and didn't recover."
Fiori, who was not in the top 150 money-winners entering the tournament, had four birdies and two bogeys in the final round.
"I never got hung up watching Tiger," Fiori said about his 20-year-old playing partner.
"I'm proud of myself for sticking to my game. They (the gallery) were pulling for Tiger and I was, too. You kind of root your playing partner on. This has got to be disappointing to him."
Magee had nine birdies and a bogey in a final round of 62 that was one off the course record set by Mike Smith in 1987.
Chris Perry and U.S. Open champion Steve Jones were three shots back at nine-under 271, while Woods fell into a tie with Jeff Maggert, Hugh Royer III and Phil Blackmar at 272.

Woods birdied the second hole and recovered from his quadruple-bogey with a birdie at number six. But he stumbled with a double-bogey at the seventh and had back-to-back bogeys at 11 and 12 to wipe out four more birdies.
"Golf is one of those games, you have to be patient," Woods said. "It's a reflection of life. I'm sure I learned a lot today. I'll have a better understanding when I look back in a couple of days."

Still, it was the first top-10 professional finish for the three-time U.S. Amateur Champion, who needs a win or approximately $60,000 in the remaining PGA events to receive a Tour exemption for next year.
